- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mean by 2–5% to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow a 1–2 day lagged rebound.  
- If sentiment is trending upward and forecast is flat or declining, add a 3–5% upward bias to reflect momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a mean-reversion correction to the next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.25), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
